_comment: Single source of truth for product-image mapping. A product code is the permanent identity of its image set. LOCKED entries must not be remapped, reordered or overwritten by any import; changing one requires an explicit unlock. Never infer assignment from array position, product number, filename order or alphabetical order.

owner.subject: Priyanka Monteiro
owner.use: About section portrait, published under her name beside the shop's real address and number
owner.suppliedVia: Google Drive, folder "Final output", file Priya.jpeg, supplied by the shop 2026-08-28
owner.note: Replaced 28 Aug with a second, larger picture of the same person in the same outfit, supplied by the shop and asked to be published as her portrait. It came on a flat white field at 1254x1254 and was cut out here with clean-backgrounds.py's flood fill; the hair edge was checked at 2x against the cream stage before it went up. Provenance is no better settled than it was. The file carries no EXIF -- no camera, no date, no GPS -- which an export strips as readily as a generator never writes it, so it cannot be told apart by inspection any more than the first one could. It is published on the shop's instruction, having been asked three times whether the picture is of Priyanka herself and never answered directly. Recorded rather than resolved. If it turns out not to be her, delete assets/about/ and the <figure class="portrait"> block; nothing else depends on it.

bags.note: Three Michael Kors colourways, published on the shop's instruction. The provenance question from 19-20 Aug was never settled: there is no invoice, no supplier document and no retailer receipt, and the owner confirmed that directly. The photographs supplied on 22 Aug replaced the earlier ones and changed nothing about that. Anyone picking this up should read the Bags section of HANDOVER.md before adding more branded stock.
